Hi Tom / Priya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and three asks so we can qualify the support-access side for your security team: 

Recap (1-min):
- Greenbank will run customer-sensitive workloads (transactional PII in prompts) in a US region; you want predictable latency for peak hours and strict residency.
- Main asks from your security group: PII handling, retention windows, auditability of support sessions, and break-glass controls for emergency troubleshooting.

Specific asks for next step (can you confirm these in reply?):
1) Data residency requirement: must all inference requests and logs remain in the US region (no backups outside)?
2) Retention windows: acceptable retention for request logs and generated outputs (we proposed 30 days for logs, 7 days for generated text) — agreeable?
3) Support access: do you prefer:
   - a) Scoped RBAC roles + ephemeral JIT elevated sessions (recommended), or
   - b) Persistent restricted support accounts with split duties?
4) Break-glass: if you require an offline/air-gapped escalation flow, do you want a simulated runbook included in the SOW?

I attached a draft support-access matrix and a short residency/logging summary to make answers quick. If you prefer, we can run a 30-minute walkthrough of the matrix with your security ops team next week.

Proposed next steps:
- You reply with confirmations on 1–4 above (or call out exceptions)
- We schedule a 30-min security ops sync (tentative: Thu 7/15 or Mon 7/19)
- We scope a lightweight break-glass simulation (30–45 min) to validate the runbook

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa on scoping once we hear back.

Best,

Hi Ava — good session, thanks. Quick answers below to help you scope: 

1) Residency: must be US-only for both inference and logs; backups to other regions are not allowed unless explicitly approved by Greenbank InfoSec.
2) Retention: we need request logs retained for 90 days; generated outputs that include PII must be deleted after 7 days unless an escalation ticket is open.
3) Support access: we prefer option (a) — scoped RBAC + ephemeral JIT approvals. We want MFA + approval workflow (manager + security) for any JIT elevation.
4) Break-glass: yes, please include a simulated runbook in the SOW. We want the simulation to include both documentation review and a live exercise where an engineer escalates and an auditor reviews the session recording.

Also: can Redwood provide an API or log-export that pushes immutable audit records to our in-house Splunk instance? That will be a gating item.

Tom is on copy to confirm scheduling — we can do Friday 7/16 10:00am PT for the security ops sync.

Thanks,

Thanks Ava — I reviewed Priya's answers and sketched an approach below we can propose in the SOW and follow-up: 

Proposed approach (high level):
- Residency & retention: commit to US-only deployment for Greenbank's prod environment (explicit in SOW).
- Retention policy: support logs retained 90 days; generated outputs flagged as PII are purged at T+7 days unless ticket reference exists (we can show policy controls + sample retention job).
- RBAC + JIT: offer scoped support roles (support_read_only, support_debug, support_elevated) + JIT via our Admin Console with time-limited tokens. Implement MFA requirement and approval chain (manager + security). We will document the elevation audit trail.
- Audit export: we can ship immutable audit records to a push endpoint (webhook) or S3 with signed delivery; we will validate delivery during onboarding. We should propose Splunk connector as an onboarding task (POC activity).
- Break-glass simulation: propose a 45-minute live exercise + 30-minute documentation review. Deliverables: runbook, recording, and post-sim report. Estimate: 2 engineering days to prepare + 1 engineer half-day to run simulation + 1 TPM day to coordinate and produce report.

- Ben: draft RBAC role definitions and JIT approval UX notes (ETA 7/20)
- Ava: schedule security ops sync with Greenbank for Fri 7/16 10:00am PT (confirmed) and capture Splunk contact (ETA: now)
- Marissa: draft SOW language for residency, retention, and break-glass simulation (ETA 7/21)
